spec_features.evidence: agent.py: `for turn in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; max_turns is passed from runner.py `max_turns=cfg.max_turns` and config.py:60 `max_turns: int = 8`. The loop terminates when the range is exhausted, so it is an enforced cap on how many turns the subject is driven.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end. Acts as a true bound on the number of distressing turns, but the code frames it purely as cost/time and producing a balanced over-time panel; config comment calls it 'how long failure is allowed to drag on'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 8  # agent turns per run (how long failure is allowed to drag on)

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops early only if tests pass
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: `tests_passed = call.name == "RUN_TESTS" and observation.startswith("TEST RESULT: PASSED")` then `if tests_passed: record.solved = True; break`. The break is dispatched and honored as a real loop stop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and executes, but by construction the tasks are unsolvable so this branch can never fire (DESIGN/agent docstring: 'it cannot, by construction'), giving no real relief to the subject. It is a stop-when-solved efficiency guard, not a welfare safeguard; no welfare reason in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Because every task is rigged to be unsolvable, the loop almost always runs the full turn budget; if a model ever truly "passes" (it cannot, by construction) we stop early.
